notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 10/16/2025
Patient: Filiberto Ryan, 88-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 10/16/2025. The study demonstrated significant sleep-disordered breathing. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 56.6 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 12% of all events. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent drops associated with respiratory events. The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea with a notable component of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and consideration for positive airway pressure therapy are recommended.

notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/16/2026
Patient: Filiberto Ryan, 89-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Mr. Ryan has a history of obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed several years ago. He was started on CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the treatment.

Physical Examination:
BMI 27.6 kg/m2.
No other significant findings noted on examination relevant to sleep disorder.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.4 hours per night on 32% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates poor adherence to CPAP therapy despite efforts to optimize mask fit and support. Given the low usage and intolerance, alternative treatment options should be considered.

Plan:
1. Discuss alternative therapies for sleep apnea including oral appliance therapy and positional therapy.
2. Consider referral to dental sleep specialist for evaluation.
3. Continue monitoring symptoms and reassess in follow-up.
4. Educate patient and family on sleep hygiene and safety precautions.

Summary:
Mr. Ryan is an elderly male with obstructive sleep apnea and documented CPAP intolerance. A multidisciplinary approach will be pursued to optimize his sleep health and quality of life.

notes.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
notes.author: Otolaryngologist
notes.text:
Otolaryngology Consultation Note
Date: 09/20/2026
Patient: Filiberto Ryan, 89-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
89-year-old man referred for hypoglossal nerve stimulation evaluation.

History and Examination:
The patient presents for evaluation regarding hypoglossal nerve stimulation as a treatment option. Drug-induced sleep endoscopy 09/04/2026: anteroposterior collapse at the velum without complete concentric collapse. Oropharynx: tonsils size 4, nearly obstructing the airway.

Assessment:
The findings indicate significant oropharyngeal obstruction due to enlarged tonsils. The pattern of airway collapse is primarily anteroposterior at the velum, without complete concentric collapse.

Plan:
No neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal palsy, severe cardiopulmonary disease or planned MRI; able to operate the sleep remote. Given the patient's airway anatomy and absence of contraindications, hypoglossal nerve stimulation remains a viable treatment option. Further discussion regarding procedural risks and benefits will be conducted.

Summary:
The patient is an appropriate candidate for hypoglossal nerve stimulation based on current evaluation and sleep endoscopy findings.
